summary: Billund Airport is the second-largest airport in Denmark, located in the heart of the Jutland peninsula. It is famously associated with the LEGO Group, whose headquarters and original factory are situated in Billund, and it serves as the primary gateway to the nearby Legoland Billund Resort. The airport also operates a military section shared with the Danish Air Force, making it a dual civilian-military facility.
faqs:
Q: How far is Billund Airport from Legoland?
A: Legoland Billund Resort is only about 2 km from the airport and easily reachable by taxi, shuttle, or a short walk.

Q: What airlines operate from Billund Airport?
A: Billund is served by several major carriers including SAS, Norwegian, Ryanair, easyJet, and Lufthansa, offering connections across Europe.

Q: Does Billund Airport have overnight stays?
A: Yes, the airport operates extended hours, and several hotels are located within minutes of the terminal, including the Hotel Legoland nearby.

Q: Are there duty-free shops at Billund?
A: Yes, the terminal features duty-free shopping, cafes, and restaurants in both the public and airside areas.
transport_tips: Billund Airport is well-connected by road via the E45 motorway, with direct bus services to major Danish cities including Aarhus, Copenhagen, and Odense. Taxis and rental cars are readily available outside the terminal, and many visitors heading to Legoland can walk or take a short shuttle ride. Parking is available on-site with both short-stay and long-stay options.
local_tip: If you have a layover or extra time, the original LEGO factory and its adjacent visitor area (LEGOLAND House) offer a quick but uniquely Danish experience right next to the airport grounds.
